# 1.2.45 - the module on a phone, and four states that were not being kept

Two things: the interface works on a tablet, a phone and a screen held
upright, and four pieces of state that could be left half-changed are kept by
one place each. No rule changed. The copy is still the copy - its rewording
comes with 1.3.0.

**A screen that is not a desk.** Foundry lays its interface out in three
columns that assume a monitor, and the module puts its own blocks in them: the
clock in the left column, the Despair rail in the top bar, the status strip and
the Projects tray in the right. Measured at every size, those columns start
colliding at about 1196 px of width and are a pile by the width of a phone -
five overlapping pairs and two blocks off the screen altogether, which is what
the photographs of it showed.

Below 1200 px the blocks leave those columns and stack in one of the module's
own instead: full width, at the top, in the order the game is read in - what
time it is, how much Despair is in the room, what is happening now, then the
table's standing and its projects. The stack scrolls rather than growing over
the map, and Foundry's own tools and the GM button start below it. The clock is
a wrapping row rather than six stacked lines, which takes it from 212 px of a
phone's 852 to about 100, and the Despair pips come down from 18 px to 13 -
enough that a pool's name, its twelve pips, its count and its stepper are one
line on the narrowest phone there is instead of leaving the stepper stranded on
a line of its own. Nothing above 1200 px changes at all.

**The glass is cut for that shape too.** The curtain reads a screen as two
bands with the filler between the columns of blocks in each, which is a desk. A
stack has no columns: every block is one full-width row at the top and the
lower half of the screen is board. Cut by the old partition, a tablet held
upright got one pane over the whole stack and two enormous shards under it.

So a stacked screen has a partition of its own, and it is built the other way
round: rather than assembling panes and checking afterwards that they tile the
screen, it starts from the screen and cuts it, and every cut is a straight line
through one convex piece. Two convex pieces and nothing else, so it holds
together by construction whatever the blocks turn out to be. Measured from
280 x 653 upwards: no overlapping panes, no gap at the screen's edge, every
block on its own pane and inside it. A row scrolled under the stack's ceiling
is cut down to the part the stack shows.

Under about 620 px of height a stacked screen keeps the theme's colour and its
type but no curtain: there is not enough of the stack left visible to cut panes
for, and the launchers in the corner come up into it. A flat backdrop stands in,
one gradient that never repaints - which also answers the fourteen frames a
second the pulse was costing in portrait. A wide short window keeps the desk's
three columns and the desk's glass; height only decides anything once the blocks
are stacked.

The interface scale is unchanged, and deliberately: its floor protects the type,
and what was too big on a phone was the layout, not the scale.

**A state is kept by one place.** Ending a trial from Edit campaign left the
trial running - the button that ends it did the closing, and the field that sets
the same phase did not. The phase owns what the phase decides now, whichever
route writes it, so the two agree; the same for an Eclipse that ends by being
switched off. The Event panel's incident card read the murder's cast from the
wrong store and vanished after the opening roll. A pane of glass with its blur
could stand over nothing after a browser tab came back, if the panel under it
left while the tab was hidden. And a new season left a running incident behind,
which is now cleared with everything else it clears.

**For the table.** If anything behaves differently after this update other than
on a narrow screen, that is a bug, and the version to compare against is 1.2.44.
